crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Expense Fraud
children.blurb: Expense fraud is the deliberate submission of false, inflated, or duplicate expense claims for reimbursement, whether by an employee, a manager, or an outside party working with an insider.

children.name: Money Laundering Networks
children.blurb: Money laundering networks are the connected sets of people, accounts, companies, and payment channels used to move and disguise the origin of criminal proceeds.

children.name: Phantom Vendors and Procurement Fraud
children.blurb: Phantom vendors and procurement fraud covers fake suppliers, shell companies, and real suppliers billing for goods or services that were never delivered.

children.name: Communication Forensics
children.blurb: Communication forensics is the examination of messages, call records, and collaboration data to reconstruct what happened, who knew what, and when.

children.name: Tracing and Recovering Digital Assets
children.blurb: Tracing and recovering digital assets covers the work of following value across blockchains and related systems after fraud, theft, ransomware, or insolvency, then trying to return it to victims or creditors.

sections.body: Fraud detection and forensics is the use of artificial intelligence to find, explain and reconstruct financial wrongdoing. In practice, systems score expense claims for odd amounts, times or merchants, and they compare invoices against vendor records to catch duplicates and fake suppliers. Graph models link accounts, devices, addresses and payments to reveal money laundering networks that rules alone would miss. Natural language models read emails, chat logs and contracts to surface pressure, collusion or intent, while blockchain analytics cluster wallet addresses and follow funds across exchanges. These tools do not replace auditors or investigators, they prioritize leads and assemble evidence for human review.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The work is mature in narrow, high volume tasks such as duplicate invoice detection, expense anomaly scoring and basic network link analysis. It is not solved in adversarial settings where fraudsters change tactics, use encrypted channels, or move value through mixers and chain hopping. False positives remain a real cost, because every alert consumes investigator time and can harm innocent customers or employees. Explainability is another limit, as a model score may not meet evidence standards without a clear audit trail. Cross border data sharing, privacy rules and model drift also constrain deployment, so most programs keep a human in the loop. The site's 219 compliance and regulation pages reflect how much of this field is shaped by reporting duties and oversight.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader can begin with Expense Fraud for employee reimbursement schemes, receipt manipulation and the anomaly models used to flag them. Money Laundering Networks covers graph analysis, layering patterns and the link charts that connect accounts, entities and transactions. Phantom Vendors and Procurement Fraud focuses on fake suppliers, invoice collusion and the controls that compare vendor master data with payment records. Communication Forensics explains how text, email and chat analysis supports timelines, intent and witness statements. Tracing and Recovering Digital Assets follows blockchain analytics, wallet clustering and exchange records used to locate and, where possible, recover value. Together these pages move from single claims to networks, from documents to communications, and from fiat trails to digital assets.
